DEPART Republic of the Philippines OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT BIYAHENG PINOY TADA' NA DILG-NAPOIßOM Building, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT HON. REXLON G. GATCHALIAN Mayor Valenzuela City Dear Mayor Gatchalian: DILG Legal Opinion No. 9 S. 2014 07 APR 2014 This refers to your 08 January 2014 letter requesting this Department's opinion on the City Government's plan to build a Local Disaster Preparedness Center which will also house the Central Fire Station and if the same is justified under 5.1.8 of Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 dated 25 March 2013. Below are the discussion relative to your query. The Statutory Basis of the LDRRMF The Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF), formerly known as the local calamity fund, is the 5% estimated revenue from regular sources which local government units are required to set aside to support disaster risk management activities pursuant to Section 324 (d) of Republic Act No. 7160, or the Local Government Code of 1991, as amended by R.A. No. 8185 and R.A. No. 10121, otherwise known as the "Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010, " viz: 'Sec. 21. Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF).- The present Incal Calamity Fund shall henceforth be known as the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF). Not less than five percent (5%) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as the LDRRMF to support disaster risk reduction and management activities, such as, but not limited to, pre-disaster preparedness programs, including training, purchasing life-saving rescue equipment, supplies and medicines, for post-disaster activities and for the payment of premiums on calamity insurance. The LDRRMC shall monitor and evaluate the use and disbursement of the LDRRMF based on the LDRMMP as incorporated in the local development plans and annual work and financial plan. Llpon the recommendation of the LDRRMO and approval of the sanggunian concerned, the LDRRMC may transfer the said fund to support disaster risk reduction work Of Other LDRRMCs which are declared under state of calamity. Of the amount appropriated for LDRRMF, thirty percent (30%) shall be allocated as Quick Fund (QRF) or stand-by fund for relief and recovery programs in order that situation and living conditions Of the people in communities or areas stricken by disasters, calamities, epidemics, or complex emergencies, may be normalized as quickly as possible.

Unexpended LDRRMF shall accrue to a special trust fund solely for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction and management activities of the LDRRMCs within the next five (5) years. Any such amount still not fully utilized after five (5) years shall revert back to the general fund and will be available for other social services to be identified by the local sanggunian. Clearly, the LDRRMF's utilization is limited to disaster risk reduction and management programs categorized into the following: (I) disaster prevention and mitigation; (2) disaster preparedness; (3) disaster response; and (4) disaster rehabilitation and recovery, including the procurement/acquisition of disaster equipment for disaster response and rescue activities under Item 5.0 of NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 (hereinafter, the "JMC") dated 25 March 2013. Whether the utilization Of. the i er ns c n Fire Stativp is justified under Item S 1.8 ofthe IMC'? Under Item 5.1.8 of the JMC, the LDRRMF may be utilized for other necessary disaster prevention and mitigation programs or projects of similar nature as those enumerated under Item 5.1.1 to 5.1.7 of the JMC, viz.: "5. I Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Disaster Prevention — refers to outright avoidance of adverse impacts Of hazards and related disaster. It expresses the concept and intention to completely avoid potential adverse impacts through action taken in advance such as construction of dams or embankments that eliminate flood risks, land-use regulations that do not permit any settlement in high risk zones and seismic engineering designs that ensure the survival and function of a critical building in any likely earthquake. Disaster Mitigation — refers to measures that would lessen or limit adverse impacts of hazards and related disasters. Mitigation measures encompass engineering techniques and hazard- resilient construction as well as improved environmental policies and public awareness. Project and Activities: 5.1.1 Conduct of risk assessment, vulnerability analysis, and other science-bayd technology and methodologies to enhance LGU ecological profile, sectoral studies and mainstream disaster risk reduction and management activities/Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) in Comprehensive [nnd use Program (CLUP) and Comprehensive Development Program (CDP);

5.1.2 Implement Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) with disaster risk reduction and management/CCA indicators; 5.1.3 Capability building (train, equip, organize, provide funding, sustain) on mainstreaming disaster risk reduction and management/CCA in development planning, investment programming/financing, and project evaluation and development; 5.1.4. Conduct activities to review and integrate disaster risk reduction and management/CCA into various environmental policies, plans, programs, and infrastructure; 5.1.5 Conduct vulnerability analysis and risk assessment for critical facilities and infrastructure; 5.1.6 Development Of tools on risk assessment; 5.1.7 Construction of dams or embankments that will reduce/mitigate flood risks; and 5.1.8 Other programs or projects of similar nature and considered necessary. " Applying the basic statutory construction principle of ejusdem generisl to Item 5.1.8 of the JMC, it appears that the specific prevention and mitigation project and activity pertaining to the construction of infrastructure which may be funded by the LDRRMF are those that are akin to or resembling the "construction of dams/embankments that will reduce/mitigate flood risks "under Item 5.1.7 thereof. In the case of Valenzuela Citys proposed utilization of the LDRRMF for purposes of constructing a Local Disaster Preparedness Center/ Central Fire Station, the same does not appear to be akin to Item 5.1.7 of the JMC and does not appear to correspond to a covered project/activity based on definition of disaster prevention and disaster mitigation which basically covers activities/projects that avoid/eliminate/lessen/limit the adverse impact of disasters. Moreover, the same does not fall under the authorized "disaster preparedness" project and activities pursuant to Item 5.2 of the JMC, which focuses on capacity building activities to enhance emergency response during disasters. However, "construction/rehabilitation of damaged infrastructure facilities and evacuation centers" are covered projects/activities classified under disaster rehabilitation and recovery of Item 5.4.2 of the JMC. Hence, construction of infrastructure facilities and evacuation centers are authorized under the JMC, viz: "5.4 Disaster Rehabilitation and Recovery xxx 5.4.2 Construction/Rehnbilitation of damaged infrastructure facilities and evacuation centers;" In addition, it should be noted that construction or rehabilitation of evacuation centers as well as facilities such as multi-purpose halls are covered social development programs under Item 3.1.4 and 3.1.9 of DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-I. As such, the 20% local development fund may be utilized for said purpose. We hope to have enlightened you on the foregoing. Very truly yours, AU ERE A. NA ERO Undersecretary DILGOUSLG
